chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Marry a free woman upon a slave girl, and do not marry a slave girl upon a free woman; and whoever marries a slave girl upon a free woman, his marriage is void.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between marrying a free woman and a slave woman as an additional wife in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchical validity of polygyny by prioritizing the status of the first wife; specifically, it permits a man to add a slave woman to his household when he already has a free wife, but declares the marriage void if he adds a free woman while already possessing a slave. This ruling reflects the classical Shia juristic view that the 'free' status holds precedence in the marital hierarchy, ensuring the social and legal standing of the primary wife is not diminished by a subsequent marriage to a slave. The narration underscores the structural integrity of the family unit within Shia fiqh, where the type of wife already present dictates the permissibility of new unions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘You can marry the free woman upon the slave girl (as an additional wife), but you cannot marry the slave girl (as an additional wife) upon the free woman; and the one who marries the slave girl (as an additional wife) upon a free woman, so his marriage is void’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

A free woman can become a second wife, the first wife being a slave-girl; but a slave-girl cannot become a second wife, the first wife being a free woman. If one marries a slave-girl as a second wife, the first being a free woman, such marriage is invalid.’”
